documents.title: Ada Lovelace biography
documents.text: Ada Lovelace was born in London in December 1815. Her father was the poet Lord Byron. She worked with Charles Babbage on the Analytical Engine and wrote a note describing an algorithm intended to be processed by the machine.

documents.title: Lord Byron biography
documents.text: Lord Byron was an English Romantic poet born in 1788. He was the father of Ada Lovelace. He died in Greece in 1824 during the Greek War of Independence.

documents.title: Charles Babbage biography
documents.text: Charles Babbage was an English mathematician and inventor born in 1791. He designed the Difference Engine and later the Analytical Engine. He is often called a pioneer of computing.

documents.title: Analytical Engine specifications
documents.text: The Analytical Engine was a proposed general-purpose mechanical computer designed by Charles Babbage. It included an arithmetic unit called the mill, memory called the store, and support for conditional branching and loops.

documents.title: Grace Hopper biography
documents.text: Grace Hopper was an American computer scientist born in 1906. She developed the first compiler and helped create the COBOL programming language. She was nicknamed Amazing Grace.

documents.title: Compiler history
documents.text: A compiler translates source code written in a high-level programming language into lower-level instructions. Grace Hopper built the A-0 compiler in 1952 for the UNIVAC I computer.

documents.title: Alan Turing biography
documents.text: Alan Turing was an English mathematician born in 1912. He described the Turing machine, a theoretical model of computation. During World War II he worked at Bletchley Park on breaking German ciphers.

documents.title: Turing machine model
documents.text: The Turing machine is an abstract model of computation introduced by Alan Turing in 1936. It reads and writes symbols on an infinite tape according to a finite table of rules.

documents.title: Marie Curie biography
documents.text: Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist born in Warsaw in 1867. She conducted pioneering research on radioactivity and discovered the elements polonium and radium with her husband Pierre Curie.

documents.title: Radioactivity research
documents.text: Radioactivity is the process by which unstable atomic nuclei release energy. Marie Curie coined the term radioactivity and won Nobel Prizes in both Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911.

documents.title: Himalaya mountain range
documents.text: The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia separating the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau. The range contains Mount Everest, the highest mountain above sea level.

documents.title: Mount Everest facts
documents.text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China. Its summit is about 8849 metres above sea level.

documents.title: Solar System overview
documents.text: The Solar System consists of the Sun and the objects orbiting it, including eight planets. Jupiter is the largest planet and has a storm called the Great Red Spot.

documents.title: Jupiter facts
documents.text: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest planet in the Solar System. The Great Red Spot is a giant storm on Jupiter that has been observed for centuries.

documents.title: Water chemistry
documents.text: Water is a chemical compound consisting of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, with formula H2O. It covers about 71 percent of Earth's surface.

documents.title: Photosynthesis process
documents.text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy. Plants use carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose and oxygen.
